entities.name: PMID:25442704
observations: McLemore et al. analyzed 5,214 open-ended abortion-care experience survey responses from 22 U.S. clinical sites using thematic analysis.
Most respondents (3,600) rated their abortion-care experience better than expected; 136 rated it worse than expected.
Women who reported worse-than-expected care primarily identified clinic-level, potentially modifiable factors, especially pain control/management and appointment or in-clinic waiting time.
The study concludes that patients’ own accounts identify specific care factors and improvement targets relevant to abortion-care quality.

entities.name: Patient experience quality
observations: In a thematic analysis of 5,214 abortion-care surveys, women’s narratives identified clinic- and patient-level factors shaping experience ratings; negative experiences chiefly implicated modifiable clinic processes and pain management.
